summary: This lecture tells of the torture of the weak who embraced Islam under Abu Jahal and Umayyah ibn Khalaf. Bilal ibn Rabah, Umayyah's slave, embraced Islam and was locked up, starved and whipped yet said only Ahad, Ahad, until Abu Bakr bought and freed him. Abu Bakr also freed the blind Zinnirah, whose sight Allah restored. Khabbab was tortured with hot iron on his back, and the family of Yasir was tortured: Sumayyah became the first martyr, Yasir died, and Ammar was forced to utter words of disbelief while his heart remained faithful, so Allah granted a concession. The ustaz closes by reminding us to be grateful for the ease of believing today and mentions the camel-entrails incident to be told later.
keyPoints: Bilal ibn Rabah was tortured by Umayyah ibn Khalaf and Abu Jahal but said only Ahad, Ahad.
Abu Bakr bought and freed Bilal, and also Zinnirah and many other slaves.
Khabbab was tortured with hot iron on his back for embracing Islam.
The family of Yasir was tortured and Sumayyah became the first martyr in Islam.
Ammar uttered words of disbelief under duress with a faithful heart, and Allah granted a concession.

chapters.title: Opening and recap
chapters.summary: The ustaz begins with Bilal's punishment, welcomes new friends, speaks of Sha'ban and continues episode 19.

chapters.title: Abu Jahal, father of wisdom
chapters.summary: Amr ibn Hisham was called Abul Hakam but called Abu Jahal by Muslims for rejecting the truth though he knew it.

chapters.title: Umayyah ibn Khalaf and Bilal
chapters.summary: Umayyah, Abu Jahal's friend, was very rich and owned many slaves, among them the strong and clever Bilal.

chapters.title: Bilal embraces Islam
chapters.summary: Bilal heard that Islam calls to the one God and embraced it secretly before Umayyah found out.

chapters.title: Locked up and starved
chapters.summary: Umayyah and Abu Jahal wanted to punish Bilal without ruining him, so they locked him up without food or drink.

chapters.title: Ahadun Ahad
chapters.summary: Though tempted with food, Bilal said only Ahad, meaning Allah is one, and was whipped all night.

chapters.title: Whipped in the middle of the road
chapters.summary: Bilal was tied on hot sand and whipped by many so people would fear to embrace Islam, yet he still said Ahad.

chapters.title: Abu Bakr buys Bilal
chapters.summary: Abu Bakr offered to buy Bilal and in the end paid a large sum, the ustaz says, then freed him. Bilal became the Prophet's personal assistant.

chapters.title: Zinnirah and Abu Quhafah
chapters.summary: Zinnirah was beaten until blind but Allah restored her sight. Abu Quhafah scolded his son for spending his wealth, but Abu Bakr sought Allah's pleasure.

chapters.title: Khabbab tortured with hot iron
chapters.summary: Khabbab, a skilled blacksmith, was tortured by Umm Anmar's thugs with hot iron on his back for refusing to leave Islam.

chapters.title: The family of Yasir
chapters.summary: Yasir, Sumayyah and their son Ammar; Ammar embraced Islam first at Dar al-Arqam before his parents.

chapters.title: The torture of the family of Yasir
chapters.summary: The family was tortured by Abu Jahal. The Prophet SAW told them to be patient and promised paradise, and Sumayyah died as the first martyr.

chapters.title: Ammar is forced to speak
chapters.summary: Ammar said he renounced Muhammad out of fear but his heart stayed faithful, and Allah revealed a verse permitting that concession.

chapters.title: Bilal's answer and Khabbab's back
chapters.summary: Bilal said he knew only one word about Allah and liked seeing Quraysh angry. Khabbab showed his back to Umar, who wept.

chapters.title: A paradise beyond imagining
chapters.summary: The last person to enter paradise gets fifty times the earth, and the first even more.

chapters.title: To be told later
chapters.summary: After Abu Talib's death camel entrails were laid on the Prophet SAW during prayer, and Umar would embrace Islam after hearing him recite the Quran.

dalil.context: The ustaz explains that Allah allowed the severely tortured to say what Quraysh demanded provided the heart stays faithful.
dalil.translation: With the exception of those who are forced to say they do not believe, although their hearts remain firm in faith, those who reject God after believing in Him and open their hearts to disbelief will have the wrath of God upon them and a grievous punishment awaiting them.
The Prophet SAW passed and saw the family of Yasir tortured and told them to be patient, for their place is paradise.
dalil.context: The ustaz relates the Prophet's words. He does not name a narrator or source.

dalil.translation: The last person to enter paradise will be given fifty times this world.
dalil.context: The ustaz relays the hadith about the reward of the last person to enter paradise. He does not name a narrator or source.

dalil.translation: The Prophet SAW said to pray as you see me pray.
dalil.context: The ustaz cites the Prophet's words about how to pray. He does not name a narrator or source.

people.context: The man who most hated the Prophet SAW and led the campaign and torture, called the Pharaoh of this nation.

people.role: Abu Jahal's friend and Bilal's master
people.context: A millionaire who tortured Bilal out of shame that his slave embraced Islam.
Said Ahad under torture, was bought and freed by Abu Bakr, then became the Prophet's personal assistant.

people.role: The first adult man to believe
people.context: Used his wealth to free tortured slaves.
Beaten until blind, her sight restored, and freed by Abu Bakr.
Scolded his son for spending his wealth on weak slaves.
Tortured with hot iron on his back, later showing his back to Umar.
Tortured for believing and died under torture.
Spat in Abu Jahal's face and was stabbed, dying as the first martyr in Islam.

people.role: Son of the family of Yasir
people.context: Embraced Islam first, was tortured and forced to utter words of disbelief with a faithful heart.

people.role: Not yet Muslim, later a companion
people.context: Would weep at Khabbab's back and ask Bilal.

sirah.era: The torture of the early companions
sirah.summary: This lecture covers the torture of Bilal, Khabbab and the family of Yasir and their freeing by Abu Bakr.

events.label: Bilal
events.title: Bilal embraces Islam
events.desc: Bilal accepted Islam secretly and Umayyah was furious on learning of it.

events.label: Whipped
events.title: Bilal is whipped
events.desc: He was whipped in the road but said only Ahad.

events.label: Bought
events.title: Abu Bakr buys Bilal
events.desc: Abu Bakr paid dearly to free him.

events.label: Zinnirah
events.title: Zinnirah's sight is restored
events.desc: Allah restored her sight after she declared that only Allah has power.

events.label: Sumayyah
events.title: Sumayyah is martyred
events.desc: She was stabbed by Abu Jahal and became the first martyr.

events.label: Ammar
events.title: Ammar is compelled
events.desc: He uttered words of disbelief out of fear but his heart stayed faithful.

lessons.title: Steadfast in tawhid
lessons.body: Bilal kept saying Allah is one despite severe torture.

lessons.title: Using wealth to free the oppressed
lessons.body: Abu Bakr bought no luxuries but used his wealth to help the tortured.

lessons.title: The sweetness of faith
lessons.body: Bilal savoured faith and did not fear people.

lessons.title: Allah gives a concession
lessons.body: One who is coerced may utter words of disbelief provided the heart remains faithful.

lessons.title: Being grateful for today's ease
lessons.body: We can easily say la ilaha illallah because the early generation sacrificed.

lessons.title: Arrogance blocks the truth
lessons.body: Abu Jahal rejected the truth though he knew it to be true.

lessons.title: Paradise beyond imagination
lessons.body: Paradise has not been seen by any eye or heard by any ear and cannot be imagined.

lessons.title: Praying as the Prophet SAW prayed
lessons.body: We pray as we see the Prophet SAW did.

glossary.meaning: One, said by Bilal because Allah is one.
Father of wisdom, the title the Arabs gave Abu Jahal.
A person owned by a master, unpaid and only given food.
One who dies defending the faith, like Sumayyah.
The Prophet's title for Abu Jahal.
